entries.detail: Rule CM-006 (Communication sheet) requires disambiguated wording with exactly one correct reading and full sentences over fragments; its SUBJECT is 'the response or transcript under review', which per the task instructions maps to the goal loop's written record, so I read GOAL_LOOP_INTERSTICE_HANGS_AND_AKIN_SOCIAL_2026-08-19_NOTES.md in full (356 lines) rather than the code targets. Two violations found. (1) Lines 68-69: 'the suite is 1,321 passed, 2 failed, 86.88% line coverage, and neither failure is in swath N1 or caused by it' uses 'neither X or Y' instead of the correct 'neither X nor Y'; a careful reader can parse this as a disjunction rather than the intended joint negation. Rewrite: '...and neither failure is in swath N1 nor caused by it:'. (2) Line 135: 'The reading rung also needs a Chromium-family browser that opens a debugging port, it tries every installed browser rather than the first that exists' is a comma splice with an ambiguous pronoun: 'it' could bind to the nearer noun phrase 'a Chromium-family browser' (nonsensical, since one browser cannot try other browsers) or, as intended, to 'the reading rung'. This is exactly the fragment/run-on pattern the rule flags. Rewrite: 'The reading rung also needs a Chromium-family browser that opens a debugging port. The rung tries every installed browser rather than the first that exists (test/reader.test.js:349), and doctor fails the rung with a specific remedy for each of browser, port and session (test/doctor-reading-rung.test.js).' I read the document end to end for this check; other explanatory passages (0.4, 0.3, 4.13, 9.4 points 1-3, RG.0, Z.4, 3.2, 3.3) were unambiguous full sentences and are not reported.
entries.rule_title: Unambiguous wording, full sentences, exactly one correct reading

entries.detail: Rule CM-008 ("anticipate and address follow-up queries preemptively") names its subject as "the response or transcript under review," which per the task routing means auditing it against /Users/scottlydon/Developer/GOAL_LOOP_INTERSTICE_HANGS_AND_AKIN_SOCIAL_2026-08-19_NOTES.md (356 lines), the only written account of this session available to me; I read the file in full rather than any of the target repos (this rule has no code-artifact subject, so the six listed target paths were not applicable to it). I went section by section (0.4, 0.6, 0.3, 0.7, "What blocks Phase 1", "Swath N1 complete", 9.4, 9.5, RG.0, RG.18, Z.4, 4.13, 3.2, 3.3) checking, for each, what a reader's most likely next question would be and whether the answer was already sitting in the file rather than left dangling. The pattern holds throughout: e.g. line 56 ("Recorded because it is the same wall loop 8 hit... it will not clear itself") preempts "why record this instead of just fixing it"; lines 265-266 and elsewhere in Z.4 preempt "why weren't the titles renamed too" with "renaming them would break every inbound reference... for a cosmetic gain"; lines 322-330 (the 4.13 harness finding) preempt "is this a new class of bug" by tying it explicitly to the existing fatalError-truncation prevention entry; RG.18 (lines 237-246) preempts "what about the other 17 sheets" by stating they each have a named item above. Several section headers are themselves built to answer the obvious next question ("4.13 closed, and why it was open"; "3.3 not ticked, and what happened instead"). I did not find a section where an obvious next question had an already-available answer left unstated; the closest candidate (3.3, lines 345-356, not stating whether item 3.1's downstream items need updating for the renamed branch) is itself flagged as an open decision rather than a completed claim, so there is no already-available answer being withheld.
